newsitem.title: NORWAY: Merrill Lynch raises view on Storebrand.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch raises view on Storebrand.

text.p: Investment house Merrill Lynch said on Monday it had raised the intermediate term recommendation for Norway's Largest insurer Storebrand ASA to accumulate from neutral.
Merrill Lynch said it believed that Storebrand's failure to agree a merger with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA could prompt further corporate activity.

At an extraordinary general meeting on June 26 two of Storebrand's major shareholders -- conglomerate Orkla ASA and private investor Kjell Inge Roekke -- voted against a fusion with Christiania Bank, effectively blocking the proposal.

"We note with interest that leading shareholder, Mr Roekke, helped block the merger. Roekke's shareholding is mainly in the voting preference shares (43 percent -- 11.5 percent of total share capital) which are due to be redeemed in 1998," Merrill Lynch said in a new analysis.
"Under the merger terms, preference shareholders would have received around NOK 14.5 per pref in 1998 against the NOK 12.1 they will receive if Storebrand remains independent," it said.
The investment house said it gave a fair price for the stock at 43 crowns per share. At 1220 GMT, Storebrand was trading unchanged at 44.50 crowns.
It said that if Storebrand were valued at the price that Den norske Bank (DnB) paid for Vital Forsikring and Storebrand's target profitability in non-life, it obtained a value to 60 crowns per share.
"We believe that there is potential for this value to be relaised for shareholders," the analysis said.
